name: Clean company profiles with HubSpot and HTTP / REST API automatically for Follow-ups

nodes.name: Weekly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — weekly. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Pull Side A (HubSpot)
nodes.notes: Looks up an existing HubSpot contact by last-modified date — finds records the pipeline hasn't processed yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Pull Side B (Airtable)
nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Contacts' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Diff the Two Systems
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.name: Create Missing in Airtable
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Contacts' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Count In-Sync Rows
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Apply Updates to Airtable
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Contacts' table, matched on contactId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Backfill into HubSpot
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Gather Sync Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Clean company profiles: Airtable

**Pattern:** Data Enrichment · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers follow-ups work end to end across Airtable and HubSpot.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Pull Side A (HubSpot)
3. Pull Side B (Airtable)
4. Diff the Two Systems
5. Create Missing in Airtable
6. Count In-Sync Rows
7. Apply Updates to Airtable
8. Backfill into HubSpot
9. Gather Sync Results

## Why it exists

Doing follow-ups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Pull Side A (HubSpot) → Pull Side B (Airtable) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in Airtable → Count In-Sync Rows → Apply Updates to Airtable → Backfill into HubSpot → Gather Sync Results

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and HubSpot aligned by hand for follow-ups
- Reconciling Airtable against HubSpot after the two quietly drifted apart
- Follow-ups work where "Pull Side A (HubSpot)" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Follow-ups work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and HubSpot in step for follow-ups, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares Airtable against HubSpot before writing, so only genuine differences land
- A failed Airtable or HubSpot call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this follow-ups build
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for follow-ups before wiring Airtable
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for follow-ups

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; HubSpot private-app token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your follow-ups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.

**Do not log**
follow-ups payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
